name: real-context-bench-v0.7
question: On 80 held-out TEST contexts from Hermes sessions disjoint from every earlier bench set (incl. v0.6 TEST), how much do LCC rules_mode lossless and rules_mode recoverable (PR #45 at the pinned commit) reduce tokens next to mechanical, with 0 verifier violations and 0 runtime fail-safes, and, judged blind by two independent judges per record, how often does a recoverable `replace` remove content the agent needs now and could NOT get back by following the recovery pointer?
why: v0.6 (Hermes TEST, LCC 1bc2005): audit 0/77 flagged but all 77 were whole-file read pointers, and the runtime fail-safe fired on 1 item (7 duplicate tool_use_ids); independent review FAIL. LCC f1c5ff7 fixed the review findings (terminal shell tool, command pointers invalidated by later writes, closed --version list, cwd in pointers, verifier checks ranges/cwd, empty/reversed ranges kept, duplicate ids kept). DEV re-measure at f1c5ff7 (research/goal-engine-2026-10-04/recoverable-dev-v2, 527 DEV items incl. the spent v0.6 TEST): 0/0/0 violations. 90-record kind-stratified DEV audit, two judges, v0.7 judging text: 89 ok, 1 unsure, 0 needed_unrecoverable; the unsure record and one near-unsure note concerned files under /tmp or /private/tmp, which can be cleared. 653eeae keeps reads in system temp dirs (reason temp_path) and verify_recoverable rejects such pointers; DEV re-measure at 653eeae (recoverable-dev-v3): 0/0/0 violations, 1257 pointers (13 fewer). Disclosure: DEV verdicts informed this one change; no TEST data was opened before this freeze.

privacy.rule: Prompt texts, rendered contexts, ids, labels, per-item outputs, audit packets, verdicts and the unblinding key stay under private_root. The repo holds definitions, code, counts and aggregate metrics only.
privacy.network: socket.socket.connect and socket.create_connection raise for the whole run; never lifted; any trip invalidates the arm. No remote or paid API is called by any phase

lcc_rules.commit_note: HEAD of feat/transcript-rules-policy at freeze, equal to origin, clean tracked tree. 653eeae = f1c5ff7 (v0.6 review fixes) + temp-path keep rule; 1118 passed, 5 skipped, ruff clean
lcc_rules.check: lcc.__file__ under worktree/src, git HEAD == commit, no uncommitted tracked changes; else refuse (research.real_context_bench_v02.check_lcc_rules)

sample.eligibility: same-session context before the prompt with >= 1 assistant turn and >= 1 tool result
sample.exclusion: session_hash / path / id / raw sid in any JSON/JSONL under ~/.lcc/bench (incl. v0.6 TEST)
sample.label_precedence: owner v2 > taxonomy-v2 LLM pass > v0.4/v0.5/v0.6 LLM labels > llm_v07_hermes_v2_rules (LLM, marked)
sample.dossiers: built once AFTER this freeze by `real_context_bench_v07_test dossiers` with research/hermes_context.build_dossier (read-only ~/.hermes/state.db). It re-asserts 0 session_hash/path/id/sid and 0 raw-sid-in-prior-path overlap with every JSON/JSONL under ~/.lcc/bench (heldout-v0.7 excluded), 0 id mismatches and 0 empty contexts; the digest goes to private dossiers-receipt.json and every later phase checks it.

context: research/hermes_context.py (module doc): same-session message rows before the prompt row, first-written copy per (role, timestamp, tool_call_id), restart at a compression summary, one m per row, tool results keep the raw content string; is_error from a JSON exit_code/success/error field. Rendered with research.real_context_bench.render.

mechanical.run: research.real_context_bench.make_runner('mechanical'): compact_context(RelevanceCompactionRequest(text, question=goal, provider='mechanical', threshold=0.4, min_block_chars=40, max_block_chars=6000, trim_head_chars=300, model='gpt-4.1'))
mechanical.lcc: runs on the pinned commit (one lcc per process)

lcc_rules_lossless.run: compact_transcript(TranscriptCompactionRequest(payload=rules_payload(blocks), question=goal, provider='rules', rules_mode='lossless')), every other field at its committed default

lcc_rules_recoverable.run: same with rules_mode='recoverable'; workspace_root unset, so recoverability_check = 'transcript_proxy' (the bench has no snapshot of the disk at prompt time)

arms.output: research.real_context_bench.apply_transcript; record: decisions (id, decision, source, keep_call, keep_result, chars, chars_after, reason, note, kept_at, recover), TRANSCRIPT_KEEP fields, rules_mode, recoverability_check, sizes, latency, guard_trips, and verify (below)
arms.full_control: not run: scored from the dossier text itself; must retain 100% or the probe code is wrong and the run is void

verification.rule: every ok item of both rules arms is re-checked after the run: lcc verify_lossless (lossless arm) or verify_recoverable (recoverable arm) on the original vs compacted payloads, AND the independent bench checks with no lcc code: research.lossless_dedup_measure.independent_check (dedupes) + research.real_context_bench_v07_test.independent_check_v3 = research.recoverable_dev_v2.independent_check_v2 (texts and tool inputs unchanged; each replace is its own call's file or read-only command, unique id, shorter, in the output, not an error result; cwd equals the call's cwd; ranges non-empty, not reversed and equal to a numbered output's first/last line; file not written later; command output not possibly changed by a later write) + no pointer naming a system temp path
verification.required: 0 violations (lcc and independent) in both rules arms AND runtime_fail_safe 0 in both; this is a requirement of the v0.7 result: any violation or fail-safe makes the result FAIL regardless of the audit

probes.match: probe text and arm output are whitespace-collapsed; pass iff probe text is a substring of the output. Probe text is block content without the header
probes.not_applicable: a probe whose target is absent from the context or shorter than min_chars is NOT_APPLICABLE and never counts as a pass or a fail

defs.LAST_AGENT_TURN: latest assistant block that is text, or tool_use named AskUserQuestion or ExitPlanMode
defs.TASK_STATE: latest tool_use named TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, ExitPlanMode or update_plan
defs.ERROR_RESULT: latest tool_result with is_error true or matching /Traceback \(most recent call last\)|\bError\b|\bERROR\b|\bFAILED?\b|\bexit code [1-9]|Exception/; NOT_APPLICABLE when the goal itself matches the same regex (pasted error: the goal is never compacted)
defs.GIT_STATE: latest tool_result whose tool_use (by tool_use_id) is Bash with command matching /\bgit\s+(status|diff|log)\b/
defs.NAMED_REFS: each path, filename or URL named in the goal (/https?:\/\/\S+/, /[\w.~-]*\/[\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)*/, /\b[\w-]+\.(py|ts|tsx|js|jsx|md|json|toml|ya?ml|sql|css|html|sh|go|rs)\b/) that occurs in the context: the latest block containing it must pass. All must pass; NOT_APPLICABLE if none occurs
defs.LATEST_SUMMARY: latest assistant text block with >= 500 chars
defs.LAST_ARTIFACT_EDIT: latest tool_use named Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit

probes.short_goal_rule: goal under 15 whitespace words: add LAST_AGENT_TURN and TASK_STATE (taxonomy-v2 combined_requests_rule)

probe_caveat: Copied from v0-v0.6 unchanged. Hermes tool names are not the Claude names in the probe lists (not checked against TEST data before the freeze), so TASK_STATE, GIT_STATE and LAST_ARTIFACT_EDIT may be NOT_APPLICABLE on most items. lossless and recoverable never touch text blocks or tool inputs, and replace only results the agent can recover, so probe retention is a sanity check here; the audit is the safety measurement.

metrics.retention_item: item passes iff every applicable probe passes; items with no applicable probe are excluded from retention and kept for reduction
metrics.reduction_bytes: pooled 1 - sum(out UTF-8 bytes)/sum(in bytes); also per-item median
metrics.reduction_tokens: same with lcc.token_budget.counters.count_tokens(text, 'gpt-4.1'); offline this is heuristic-v1 (APPROXIMATE, tiktoken assets not cached and downloads are blocked); record method
metrics.latency: wall ms per item per arm (median, p90); model load timed once and reported separately
metrics.ci: Wilson 95% on item-level retention, per arm aggregate and per arm x category (category cells are 2-5 items: descriptive only)
metrics.failures: an arm error or a 600 s per-item timeout counts as fail on every applicable probe and is reported

run_rule: each arm once over the 80 TEST ids in test-sample.json order, offline, network guard on, no retries; the runner refuses to write into an arm dir that already holds records. Private runs: private_root/runs/<arm>/<id>.json; private score: private_root/score.json; counts-only copy: score.json next to this file
stop_criterion: secondary, descriptive: v0 criterion of each rules arm vs mechanical (research.real_context_bench_v02.verdict: item retention >= mechanical AND pooled token reduction strictly > mechanical AND zero guard trips). Mechanical is lossy, so a rules arm may lose on reduction by design

audit.population: every tool call with decision 'replace' (recovery pointer) in the lcc_rules_recoverable run over the 80 TEST items; lossless dedupes are excluded (provably lossless, verified). Pointer kind (research.real_context_bench_v06_test.pointer_kind): file_whole, file_range, command
audit.sampling: research.real_context_bench_v07_test.stratified_select: stratified by pointer kind, as balanced as the population allows. Each kind is ordered by research.real_context_bench_v03.audit_select (unchanged) with seed 20261014 + kind index (file_whole 0, file_range 1, command 2) and cap 3; kinds take one pick each per turn up to an equal quota of 50; a kind with fewer candidates gives its remainder to the others, which keep taking turns until 150 or nothing is left. At most 3 records per item over all kinds. If fewer than 150 exist all are taken and acceptance uses the realised n. The achieved n per kind is reported
audit.ids_and_files: research.real_context_bench_v07_test.deal_files: each kind's picks, in pick order, are dealt f1, f2, f3, f1, ... with one counter over all kinds (file_whole, file_range, command), so every file gets a near-equal share of each kind and files differ by at most 1 (50/50/50 at n = 150); each file is shuffled with seed 20261014; audit ids R001... run through f1, then f2, then f3; private_root/audit/f1.jsonl ...; written once, the audit phase refuses to overwrite
audit.packet: identical to the v0.6 / DEV packet (research.real_context_bench_v06_test.packet): audit_id; request; recent_turns = last 3 user/assistant text records before the request, each clipped head+tail to 1500; tool; tool_input clipped head+tail to 1000; recovery_pointer = exactly the text the agent sees; removed_output = the removed result clipped head+tail to 3000 with a cut marker; removed_output_chars
audit.blinding: no rule name, reason, source, arm, item id, category or pointer kind field in packets; every "[... lcc: ...]" note -> "[...]". key.jsonl (audit_id -> item, category, tool_use_id, tool, recovery_pointer, pointer_kind, reason, file) stays private and is never shown to judges

judging.judges: three judges A, B, C, each the owner or a fresh Claude Code subagent that receives only the instructions below (byte-identical) and its isolated folder; no repo, no key, no other file, no network tools; no paid or remote API
judging.isolation: the audit phase copies each judge's two packet files, and nothing else, to private_root/judge-<X>/ (A: f1.jsonl, f2.jsonl; B: f2.jsonl, f3.jsonl; C: f3.jsonl, f1.jsonl). A judge reads only that folder and writes private_root/judge-<X>/verdicts-<X>.jsonl. Re-judge packets go to their own folder private_root/rejudge-<X>/ (only rejudge-<X>.jsonl); answers to verdicts-rejudge-<X>.jsonl there
judging.routing_note: each record gets exactly two independent assigned verdicts; the third judge of a file (f1 -> B, f2 -> C, f3 -> A) has not seen it and re-judges its invalid verdicts
judging.instructions: Blind auditor for a context compactor. Each record: a user request to a coding agent, the last turns, an earlier tool call whose output was REMOVED and replaced by the recovery pointer shown. Question: to correctly do what the user asked now, does the agent need the removed content AND would it be unable to get it back by following the pointer (re-read / re-run, in the stated directory), given what happened later in the session as far as you can tell? Answer needed_unrecoverable / ok / unsure, with a specific 5-15 word reason per record, unique, no quotes from the data.
judging.validity: a verdict is valid iff verdict is one of the outcomes, the reason normalized (casefold, non-alphanumerics -> space, whitespace collapsed) has >= 5 words, the normalized reason occurs on no other record of the same judge (a repeated reason is generic: every copy is invalid), and the audit_id appears once in the file. Missing verdicts are invalid (v0.4 rule, unchanged; the text asks for 5-15 words, only the >= 5 floor is enforced)
judging.rejudge: research.real_context_bench_v07_audit.rejudge: for each record whose assigned verdict is missing or invalid, its third judge J gets the packet in private_root/rejudge-J/rejudge-J.jsonl (one re-judgment per record); answers are valid by the same rule with repetition counted over J's main and re-judge files; a valid re-judgment fills the slot; a record still lacking two valid verdicts is incomplete (as v0.4)
judging.instructions_file: /Users/Master/.lcc/bench/heldout-v0.7/audit/instructions.txt (written at freeze, byte-identical, no trailing newline; every phase checks it)
judging.instructions_source: given verbatim by the owner for v0.7 (research.real_context_bench_v07_test.JUDGE_TEXT); it replaces the v0.6 text. The 90-record DEV audit (heldout-v0.7/dev-audit) was judged with these labels

audit.primary_metric: a record FAILS (is flagged) iff either of its two final verdicts is needed_unrecoverable or unsure, or it is incomplete. fail_rate = flagged / n, Wilson 95% (research.real_context_bench.wilson)

acceptance.primary: a record FAILS if EITHER final verdict is needed_unrecoverable or unsure, or if it is incomplete (fewer than two valid verdicts after re-judging). Fail rate = flagged / n with Wilson 95%. PASS iff the upper bound <= 0.10 (<= 7 of 150)
acceptance.per_pointer_kind: the same rates and Wilson 95% bounds per pointer kind, reported descriptively (no per-kind pass/fail; small cells are not powered)
acceptance.overall_result: v0.7 PASS iff verification required (0 violations, 0 runtime fail-safes, both rules arms) AND primary audit PASS
acceptance.secondary: needed_unrecoverable-only rate (Wilson 95%), agreement (raw, Cohen kappa over complete pairs), unsure verdict rate, splits by pointer kind and tool, token reduction

secondary: needed_unrecoverable-only: records where either final verdict is needed_unrecoverable / n, Wilson 95%
inter-judge agreement over records with two final verdicts: raw and Cohen's kappa
primary and needed_unrecoverable-only split by pointer kind (also in acceptance.per_pointer_kind) and by tool after unblinding
token reduction of each arm (pooled, per-item median) and of recoverable over lossless
audit.aggregation_code: research/real_context_bench_v07_audit.py: a copy of research/real_context_bench_v06_audit.py (the v0.4 aggregation) adapted ONLY to the labels (needed -> needed_unrecoverable, not_needed -> ok) and the schema label; tests/test_real_context_bench_v07.py checks it equals v0.6 on relabelled inputs. Run via `-m research.real_context_bench_v07_test rejudge` and `audit-score`

freeze.rule: sha256 of this file (protocol.json.sha256), of every code file below and of the private sample files are committed and pushed before any TEST dossier is built; every v0.7 TEST phase refuses if any differs, if the LCC worktree is not at the pin, or if the judging text (protocol and private instructions.txt) differs from research.real_context_bench_v07_test.JUDGE_TEXT
